q: In 2 Corinthians, Paul says anyone in Christ is a new what?
quote: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.

q: In 2 Corinthians, Paul says we walk by faith, not by what?
why: We trust what we cannot see.
quote: For we walk by faith, not by sight.

q: In 2 Corinthians, what kind of giver does God love?
quote: For God loves a cheerful giver.

q: In 2 Corinthians, the Lord told Paul, “My grace is sufficient for…”
why: His power is perfected in weakness.
quote: My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.

q: In 2 Corinthians, Paul says, “When I am weak, then I am…”
quote: For when I am weak, then I am strong.

q: In 2 Corinthians, Paul calls God the God of all what?
why: He comforts us in all troubles.
quote: the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort

q: In 2 Corinthians, Paul says we have this treasure in jars made of what?
why: The power is from God, not us.
quote: Now we have this treasure in jars of clay

q: In 2 Corinthians, Paul says believers are ambassadors for whom?
quote: Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ

q: In 2 Corinthians, how many times did Paul say he was shipwrecked?
why: He suffered much for the gospel.
quote: three times I was shipwrecked.

q: How does Paul close 2 Corinthians?
quote: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.

q: In 2 Corinthians, why does God comfort us in our troubles?
quote: so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves have received from God.

q: In 2 Corinthians, what is being renewed day by day?
why: So we do not lose heart.
quote: yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.

q: In 2 Corinthians, what does Paul say is eternal?
quote: For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.

q: In 2 Corinthians, Paul calls the believers a letter from Christ written on what?
why: Written by the Spirit, not ink.
quote: not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.

q: In 2 Corinthians, though Christ was rich, what did He become for our sakes?
quote: that though He was rich, yet for your sakes He became poor

q: In 2 Corinthians, whoever sows generously will also do what?
quote: and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.

q: In 2 Corinthians, what was Paul given to keep him from becoming conceited?
why: He pleaded for it to be removed.
quote: I was given a thorn in my flesh

q: In 2 Corinthians, how many times did Paul plead for his thorn to be taken away?
quote: Three times I pleaded with the Lord to take it away from me.

q: In 2 Corinthians, how did Paul escape the governor in Damascus?
why: Through a window in the wall.
quote: But I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped his grasp.

q: In 2 Corinthians, Paul asks what fellowship light has with what?
quote: Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?

q: In 2 Corinthians, in whom should anyone who boasts boast?
quote: Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.

q: Who joined Paul in greeting the church at Corinth in 2 Corinthians?
why: The letter also went to Achaia.
quote: and Timothy our brother, To the church of God in Corinth

q: In 2 Corinthians, Paul says a man in Christ was caught up to which heaven?
quote: was caught up to the third heaven.

q: In 2 Corinthians, under which king did the Damascus governor try to arrest Paul?
quote: In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas secured the city

q: In 2 Corinthians, whose arrival comforted Paul?
quote: comforted us by the arrival of Titus

q: In 2 Corinthians, how many times did Paul receive forty lashes minus one?
quote: Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.

q: In 2 Corinthians, how long did Paul say he spent in the open sea?
quote: I spent a night and a day in the open sea.
